title: Adhesive Strength of Carbon Nanotubes Grown on Various Substrates
content: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are hollow tubes of graphene. They are renowned for their exceptional mechanical strength and promising applications ranging from nanotechnology to biomedical devices. CNTs can be grown on conventional silicon substrates using catalyst layers; they can also form directly on metals such as stainless steel, potentially simplifying production and broadening usage in areas such as medical implants, where CNTs have been shown to have anti-microbial properties [1]. Despite the potentially advantageous benefits of CNTs for applications in medical implants, their detachment from the grown substrate may also pose a potential health risk. In this work, we present a method to help quantify the adhesive strength of CNTs onto various substrates, a factor critical for the use of CNTs in biomedical contexts where detachment of CNTs is unfavorable.
